title: Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery
summary: Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery's refusal to ask the Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over allegations against a minister in Western Carolinas Presbytery. The Assembly did not sustain the complaint because Western Carolinas had not refused jurisdiction. It nevertheless directed that presbytery to proceed at its next stated meeting and held the one-year limitation inapplicable because its commission had unduly delayed formal process. The ruling was conditional, not an unqualified endorsement of the handling below.

sources.supported_claims: Identifies the filing as a complaint and supports the conditional non-sustaining judgment, direction to Western Carolinas, jurisdictional reason, and limitations ruling.

source_limits: The complete adopted recommendation and grounds are available; the allegations against the minister remain allegations and were not adjudicated here.
evidence_notes: The proceeding is a complaint against Grace Presbytery's refusal to request original jurisdiction, not a BCO 34-1 request addressed directly to the Assembly.
Grace acted properly in sending the matter to Western Carolinas, but Western Carolinas had unduly delayed and was directed to proceed.
The one-year limit did not apply because Western Carolinas had appointed a judicial commission.

score_reasons.decisive_reason: States that the minister's presbytery had not refused jurisdiction.
